These references explain the statistical ideas behind the guides. A citation
is not a claim that Trex implements every estimator, assumption, inference
procedure or computational refinement in the cited work. The [API reference](reference/index.qmd)
and each guide's scope section describe the implementation actually provided.

## Regression and moment restrictions

- Hansen, L. P. (1982). **Large Sample Properties of Generalized Method of
  Moments Estimators.** *Econometrica* 50(4), 1029–1054.
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.2307/1912775).
- Newey, W. K., and K. D. West (1987). **A Simple, Positive Semi-Definite,
  Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent Covariance Matrix.**
  *Econometrica* 55(3), 703–708. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.2307/1913610).
- Newey, W. K., and R. J. Smith (2004). **Higher Order Properties of GMM
  and Generalized Empirical Likelihood Estimators.** *Econometrica* 72(1),
  219–255. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1468-0262.2004.00482.x).
- Muandet, K., W. Jitkrittum, and J. Kübler (2020). **Kernel Conditional
  Moment Test via Maximum Moment Restriction.** *UAI*.
  [Proceedings](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v124/muandet20a.html).
- **Optimal Convex M-Estimation for Linear Regression via Antitonic Score
  Matching.** The [R package `asm`](https://rdrr.io/cran/asm/) documents the
  original procedure and references. Trex ports its core score-learning idea;
  its numerical options and inferential implementation are not a claim of
  complete feature parity with the R package.

For least squares, Frisch–Waugh–Lovell projections, sandwich covariance and
identification, a graduate econometrics treatment is useful alongside the
worked code. GMM and kernel criteria require valid moments; automatic
differentiation supplies derivatives, not identifying assumptions.

## Choice and structural dynamics

- Rust, J. (1987). **Optimal Replacement of GMC Bus Engines: An Empirical
  Model of Harold Zurcher.** *Econometrica* 55(5), 999–1033.
  [DOI](https://doi.org/10.2307/1911259).
- Hotz, V. J., and R. A. Miller (1993). **Conditional Choice Probabilities
  and the Estimation of Dynamic Models.** *Review of Economic Studies*
  60(3), 497–529. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.2307/2298122).
- Train, K. (2009). **Discrete Choice Methods with Simulation**, second
  edition. [Author's book page](https://eml.berkeley.edu/books/choice2.html).
- Kallus, N., and M. Udell (2016). **Revealed Preference at Scale: Learning
  Personalized Preferences from Assortment Choices.**
  [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05113).

## Panels and low-rank structure

- Arkhangelsky, D., S. Athey, D. A. Hirshberg, G. W. Imbens, and S. Wager
  (2021). **Synthetic Difference-in-Differences.** *American Economic Review*
  111(12), 4088–4118. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20190159).
  [Reference implementation](https://github.com/synth-inference/synthdid).
- Athey, S., M. Bayati, N. Doudchenko, G. Imbens, and K. Khosravi (2021).
  **Matrix Completion Methods for Causal Panel Data Models.** *JASA*.
  [Working-paper version](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.10251).
- Mazumder, R., T. Hastie, and R. Tibshirani (2010). **Spectral Regularization
  Algorithms for Learning Large Incomplete Matrices.** *JMLR* 11, 2287–2322.
  [Article](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/mazumder10a.html).
- Bonhomme, S., T. Lamadon, and E. Manresa (2022). **Discretizing Unobserved
  Heterogeneity.** *Econometrica* 90(2), 625–643.
  [Working-paper version](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.02124).

## Generative models

- Gulrajani, I., F. Ahmed, M. Arjovsky, V. Dumoulin, and A. Courville (2017).
  **Improved Training of Wasserstein GANs.**
  [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.00028).
- Ho, J., A. Jain, and P. Abbeel (2020). **Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic
  Models.** [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239).
- Sohn and Song. **Parallelly Tempered Generative Adversarial Nets:
  Toward Stabilized Gradients.**
  See the [paper and current revision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.11786)
  for the convex tempering and coherency construction used by `TabularPTGAN`.
- Hu, E. J., et al. (2022). **LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language
  Models.** [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685).
- Dettmers, T., A. Pagnoni, A. Holtzman, and L. Zettlemoyer (2023).
  **QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs.**
  [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14314).

## Numerical references used by the repository

The test suite compares selected calculations with SciPy, Statsmodels,
linearmodels, saved R fixtures, independent finite differences and the
`synthdid` California example. See
[tests](https://github.com/apoorvalal/trex/tree/main/tests) and
[fixture provenance](https://github.com/apoorvalal/trex/blob/main/tests/data/README.md).
These checks have defined scopes; they do not establish correctness of all
possible inputs or replace an estimator-specific design and validation study.
